input.question: If Oil prices have dropped close to 40% per barrel, why has diesel only dropped 10% at the pump [UK]
input.ground_truth: Because the price at the pump isn't solely determined by price per barrel. Refining it still costs the same and the government and/or state taxes don't change. I also costs the same amount to transport. Also, 1 barrel of oil (42 gallons) translates into about 10 gallons of diesel when refined.

But here’s the thing: the candy you sell comes in different types. Some candy is easy to turn into other things, like making candy bars. But some candy is special and can only be used for one thing, like making chocolate milk.

Oil is a bit like that candy. When oil prices go down a lot, the stuff that can easily be changed (like gasoline for cars) also goes down a lot. But diesel is a bit different—it’s harder to change into something else, and there are rules about how much you can sell. Also, the people who sell you diesel at the gas station have their own costs and want to make some money too.

So, even though oil went down a lot, diesel at the pump doesn’t go down as much. It’s like your special candy doesn’t drop in price as much because it’s trickier to sell and there are other things that decide its price too!
